# Legacy v1 provider id for Azure. It has no model files of its own: v1 serves
# providers/azure's models here with this provider's env vars, and the v2 output
# leaves it out. Add or change models in providers/azure.
name = "Azure Cognitive Services"
env = ["AZURE_COGNITIVE_SERVICES_RESOURCE_NAME", "AZURE_COGNITIVE_SERVICES_API_KEY"]
npm = "@ai-sdk/azure"
doc = "https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/ai-services/openai/concepts/models"

[v1_alias]
provider = "azure"
env = { AZURE_RESOURCE_NAME = "AZURE_COGNITIVE_SERVICES_RESOURCE_NAME", AZURE_API_KEY = "AZURE_COGNITIVE_SERVICES_API_KEY" }

# Effort: output_config.effort = low|medium|high|xhigh. Foundry's effort table lists max as "No" for claude-fable-5-1 ("xhigh produces the same result as max"):

# Mid-conversation: Foundry lists "Mid-conversation role: system" (haiku-5-5, opus-5-5, opus-5, sonnet-5-5, sonnet-5) and "Per-turn effort controls" (opus-5-5, opus-5) as Beta:
# https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/foundry/foundry-models/concepts/claude-models#available-claude-models. Anthropic lists mid-conversation system messages, per-message effort and

# Microsoft's Foundry Claude page (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/foundry/foundry-models/concepts/claude-models, updated 2026-09-22) doesn't list claude-fable-5-2 yet, so this file follows Anthropic's Foundry docs.
# Prices: Foundry bills Claude in CCUs at Anthropic's standard per-model, per-feature rates: https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/about-claude/pricing#claude-in-microsoft-foundry-pricing; rates: https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/about-claude/pricing#model-pricing
# The US Data Zone 1.1x multiplier applies only to deployments hosted on Azure, which this model doesn't have.
# Cache: 1h TTL and the 512-token minimum on Foundry: https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/prompt-caching#1-hour-cache-duration, https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/prompt-caching#cache-limitations

#   (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/foundry/foundry-models/concepts/claude-models#thinking-and-effort) and doesn't cover 5.2 yet, and I couldn't test Foundry, so max is left out to match those peers.

# tools.strict/search: structured outputs and the tool search tool list Microsoft Foundry and claude-fable-5-2: https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/structured-outputs, https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/tool-use/tool-search-tool

# Mid-conversation flags left out: Anthropic lists mid-conversation system messages, tool changes and per-message effort for the Claude API, Claude Platform on AWS, Bedrock and Google Cloud, not Foundry: https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/mid-conversation-system-messages
# Fast mode is a separate Foundry model, claude-fable-5-2-fast, not added here: https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/fast-mode

# Mid-conversation (live, aiden-azury-group, 2026-10-19; probe in notes/azure-mid-conversation-probe.ts): Azure OpenAI Responses and Chat Completions accept
# system/developer messages in place; Responses accepts `additional_tools` items (https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/tools-tool-search#add-tools-at-a-specific-point-in-the-input);
# `configuration_update` returns 400 "not supported with this model" except on GPT-6 (accepted on gpt-6-luna; https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/reasoning).
# Web search: billed as Grounding with Bing Search, $14 per 1,000 Bing search requests (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/foundry/openai/how-to/web-search#web-search-usage-and-billing): https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/bing/apis/grounding-pricing
# Token-only multipliers (object factor, so cost.web_search is unscaled): web search is billed separately as Grounding with Bing Search (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/foundry/openai/how-to/web-search#web-search-usage-and-billing).
# APIs: Responses (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/foundry/openai/how-to/responses, Supported models) and Chat Completions (API and feature support tables at https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/foundry/openai/how-to/reasoning).
# Per-API flags: additional_tools (and configuration_update, where set) exist only on the Responses API, so tools.updates / effort_updates sit on [api.responses]. Mid-conversation developer messages work on both Responses and Chat Completions (OpenAI documents both; Azure Chat kept the cache live on 2026-10-23), so system_updates stays top-level.
schema = 2
base_model = "openai/o4-mini"
base_model_omit = ["structured_output"]
status = "deprecated"

[modalities]
input = ["text", "image/jpeg", "image/png", "image/gif", "image/webp", "application/pdf"]
output = ["text"]

[capabilities]
tools = { supported = true, strict = true, choice = ["auto", "none", "required", "tool"] }
reasoning = { supported = true, effort = ["low", "medium", "high"] }
store = true
cache = { implicit = { min_tokens = 1_024 } }
system_updates = true

[api.responses]
capabilities = { tools = { updates = true } }

[api.chat-completions]
sdk = { opencodeai = "@opencode/ai/providers/azure/chat" }

[cost.text.input]
price = 1.1
cache = { read = 0.275 }

[cost.text.output]
price = 4.4

[cost.web_search]
price = 14

[[cost.multipliers]]
when = { region = { in = ["us", "eu"] } }
factor = { text = 1.1 }
